landing.scienceQuote: Under volatility, feelings often decide before reflection gets a chance.
landing.scienceDesc: Research on affect and risk shows that fear in a drop or euphoria in a surge can steer choices before you've regulated. Naming what you feel and slowing down creates space for deliberate judgment — not a market call from us.
landing.scienceCitationLabel: Loewenstein, G., Weber, E. U., Hsee, C. K., & Welch, N. (2001). "Risk as feelings." Psychological Bulletin, 127(2), 267–286.
landing.scienceStepsIntro: Each step in Holzen's pause session follows a specific principle from clinical and behavioral research:
landing.scienceStepFeel: Name what you're feeling first. Putting feelings into words ('affect labeling') gives the rest of the ritual a clear emotional anchor (Lieberman et al., 2007).
landing.scienceStepBreathe: Slow breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system, shifting from fight-or-flight toward regulation so reflection lands in a steadier body state (Porges, 2011).
landing.scienceStepReflect: Engage in cognitive reappraisal. Reframing after regulation leads to better decisions than suppression or avoidance (Gross, 2002).
landing.scienceStepFrame: Choose your angle. After the reflection, open the companions that help — a metacognitive pause before commitment (Flavell, 1979).
landing.scienceStepBreatheAgain: Regulate once more before you choose. A second breathing pass lowers arousal again after reframing (Lehrer & Gevirtz, 2014).
landing.scienceStepDecide: Act from intention, not impulse. System 2 is online: move from reactive processing to a deliberate outcome (Kahneman, 2011).
landing.scienceStepsSummary: Feel, breathe, reflect, frame, breathe again, then decide — six beats, with a brief settle moment on the same final segment before you record an outcome; each maps to peer-reviewed work from Lieberman, Porges, Gross, Flavell, and Kahneman.
landing.pricingDesc: Start with a {{trialDays}}-day free trial of Pro — unlimited pauses and AI companions (${{price}}/month after, cancel anytime). When your trial ends, you can reactivate from Settings to keep pausing.

faq.whoAnswer: Anyone who invests and has felt the pull to act when markets move — whether that's selling during a drop, buying during a surge, or endlessly checking the chart. Holzen is for people who want to understand their emotional patterns and choose deliberately. It is not a signals or trading tool.
faq.adviceQuestion: Does Holzen tell me to buy, sell, or hold?
faq.adviceAnswer: No. Holzen doesn't know your goals, timeline, or portfolio. It interrupts impulse and helps you notice what you're feeling so you decide — consciously. Outcomes you log during a pause are for your own awareness, not our recommendation.
faq.breatheQuestion: I don't need an app to tell me to breathe.
faq.breatheAnswer: You're right — you don't. But Holzen doesn't just remind you to breathe. It intercepts you at the exact moment volatility hits, sequences you through a science-backed protocol (feel → regulate → reappraise → frame → regulate again → decide), and tracks your patterns over time. Willpower alone doesn't build a practice. Timing and structure do.
faq.meditationQuestion: Isn't this just another meditation app?
faq.meditationAnswer: Meditation apps are general-purpose. Holzen is triggered by real market events — it meets you in the moment you're most likely to act on impulse. It combines breathing, AI reflections, behavioral science, curated intelligence, and long-term pattern tracking into one practice. Calm doesn't know when Bitcoin just dropped 8%.
faq.valueQuestion: ${{price}}/month for something I might rarely use?
faq.valueAnswer:
The moments you use Holzen are the moments that matter most — when a single impulsive decision can cost you clarity, sleep, or capital. One pause taken at the right time is worth far more than the subscription.

How often you pause is not "once in a blue moon" by design: when markets are choppy or your thresholds are sensitive, alerts can add up to many times a month. In settings, Holzen estimates how often you would have paused on recent price action so you can tune how often you want to be interrupted instead of guessing. You can also request a pause anytime from Home without waiting for an alert, with a short cooldown so the habit stays intentional.

Your {{trialDays}}-day trial includes full Pro access. After it ends, reactivate from Settings to keep engaging with new pauses.
faq.fairUseAnswer: Pro includes unlimited pauses and AI companions for personal use — there's no per-month cap you can hit. To keep the service healthy for everyone, we apply light technical limits (a short cooldown between pauses and a per-hour ceiling) that real users never notice in practice. These only come into play for clearly abusive patterns like scripted traffic or repeated automated runs.
faq.worksAnswer: Each step follows peer-reviewed research: affect labeling (Lieberman), vagal breathing (Porges), cognitive reappraisal (Gross), metacognition (Flavell), a second regulation pass, and deliberate decision-making (Kahneman). Over time, your stats reveal patterns you can't see in the moment — and that awareness itself shifts behavior.
faq.rationalQuestion: I'm a steady investor — I don't panic.
faq.rationalAnswer: That's what most investors believe until a sharp move. Research shows even experienced people overestimate their emotional resilience. Holzen isn't just for panic — it catches subtle patterns like over-checking, quiet anxiety, or euphoric overconfidence that erode deliberate choice without you noticing.

about.opportunityBody1: The democratisation of investing is one of the most important financial shifts of our time.
about.opportunityBody2: Platforms like Robinhood, Trade Republic, and countless others have opened markets that were once reserved for professionals. Anyone can now invest in stocks, ETFs, commodities — and Bitcoin. This is a genuinely good thing.
about.opportunityBody3: But access is only half the equation. What these platforms don't provide is the emotional infrastructure to handle what comes next: the volatility, the uncertainty, the constant temptation to act when doing nothing would serve you better.
about.opportunityBody4: That's the gap Holzen fills — not with more data or faster alerts, but with a practice of self-awareness designed to create space between impulse and decision.
about.researchBody1: Markets move. Noticing your emotions under volatility is harder than it looks.
about.researchBody2: Behavioral research has documented this for decades. Daniel Kahneman's work on System 1 and System 2 thinking shows that under stress, our fast, instinctive mind hijacks decisions before our slower, reflective mind can intervene. Loewenstein and colleagues found that people often react from immediate feelings about risk before they analyze it carefully — which is exactly the gap a structured pause is meant to bridge.
about.researchBody3: This is true for experienced investors and beginners alike. The difference is that beginners often don't yet recognise the pattern: the urge to sell when prices fall, the urge to buy when prices surge. Both feel rational in the moment. Neither usually is.
about.researchBody4: Holzen applies this research directly. When volatility crosses your threshold, you're guided through a science-backed pause designed to move you from reactive to deliberate.
about.pauseResearchTitle: The science behind the guided pause ritual
about.pauseResearchIntro: Every pause session follows a sequence grounded in clinical and behavioral research — not guesswork.
about.pauseResearchFeelDesc: Naming your state first — affect labeling — gives the ritual a clear emotional anchor. Lieberman et al. (2007) show labeling interacts with arousal; Holzen sequences it before the first breathing pass.
about.pauseResearchBreatheDesc: Slow, rhythmic breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system (Polyvagal Theory, Porges 2011), preparing you to sit with the reflection.
about.pauseResearchReflectDesc: Cognitive reappraisal — reframing the situation — leads to better decisions than suppression. Gross (2002) showed reappraisal works best once intensity has been reduced.
about.pauseResearchFrameDesc: After the reflection, choose angles (companions and tools) with intention — metacognitive awareness (Flavell, 1979) before you commit.
about.pauseResearchBreathe2Desc: A second regulation pass lowers arousal again after reframing and exploration, before the outcome step.
about.pauseResearchDecideDesc: With regulation and reappraisal behind you, Kahneman's System 2 (2011) is online. You can act from intention rather than impulse.
about.readFullScience: See the full research on our landing page →
about.bitcoinBody1: Holzen launches with Bitcoin because it moves sharply, trades around the clock, and tends to stir strong emotions — an honest place to practice pausing before you act.
about.bitcoinBody2: That doesn't mean we take a view on whether you should own Bitcoin, how much, or for how long. Your strategy is yours. We watch price moves so we can meet you in volatile moments, not to judge them.
about.bitcoinBody3: Bitcoin is emotionally demanding in a way many assets are not: big swings, always-on markets, and a culture that celebrates conviction. That makes it a strong first trigger — not a claim that everyone should hold.
about.bitcoinBody4: Holzen exists to help you hold yourself — with awareness. We don't tell you what to do with your portfolio. We help you pause long enough to notice your impulse, name it, and choose deliberately.
about.philosophyBody1: Holzen is a micropreneur project — small by design.
about.philosophyBody2: We don't have investors, a growth team, or a roadmap optimised for scale. We have a focused product, a clear price, and users who value what we build.
about.philosophyBody3: We believe the best software is often built by small teams who care deeply about the problem they're solving. No engagement metrics, no dark patterns, no pressure to grow at all costs.
about.reserveBody1: Separately from the product, Holzen maintains a company Bitcoin reserve. See our reserve strategy for the founders' conviction — it's not guidance for your portfolio.
about.reserveBody2: Holzen maintains a Bitcoin reserve as a long-term store of value — not as speculation, but as a statement of founders' conviction.
about.aboutUsBody1: Holzen is built by a husband-and-wife team. We built it because investing under volatility is hard — and we wanted a practice for the moments impulse speaks loudest.
about.aboutUsBody2: We hope Holzen can do the same for you.

aboutPauses.sheetTitle: Why pause — the science behind it
aboutPauses.title: Why pause?
aboutPauses.subtitle: The science behind it

holzen.title: Holzen, in one breath
holzen.body: Holzen is a structured pause for investors: you name what you feel, slow your body with breath, then choose from a steadier state. It is not price advice — it is a regulation ritual so impulses have less room to steer. We start with Bitcoin volatility as the trigger.

challenge.title: The challenge you are in
challenge.body: Markets compress time. A chart can feel like a verdict on your judgment, your security, your future. Volatility pulls attention toward threat and reward at once — a recipe for reactive trades. Pausing widens the gap between stimulus and response.

ninety.title: The 90-second window
ninety.body: Strong emotional surges often crest within roughly 90 seconds if you do not feed them with new stories or new clicks. A short breathing sequence can help your nervous system shift out of emergency pacing so your prefrontal cortex can come back online for a deliberate choice.

mechanisms.title: Three proven mechanisms
mechanisms.body: Putting feelings into words (affect labeling) can blunt amygdala drive. Slow exhales lean on the parasympathetic side of regulation. Stepping back to reappraise — “what story am I believing?” — creates distance between you and the urge to act immediately.

sixSteps.title: The deep pause (six beats)
sixSteps.body: The header shows six beats: Feel, Breathe, Reflect, Frame, a second Breathe, then Decide. After that second breath, one short settle screen appears before you log what you chose — for your awareness only. Each beat maps to skills psychologists study: interoception, autonomic settling, perspective-taking, metacognition, re-centering, and values-aligned action.

ritual.title: Not a remedy — a ritual
ritual.body: A ritual is not a guarantee of profit. It is a repeatable way to practice composure under uncertainty. Over time, the win is fewer decisions made in the red zone of panic or euphoria — and more that match who you want to be across cycles.

pauseScience.title: Each step follows research
pauseScience.feelDesc: Labeling emotions ('affect labeling') reduces amygdala activation — but naming comes early so the rest of the ritual can work with what you named. (Lieberman et al., 2007)
pauseScience.breatheDesc: Slow breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system, shifting from fight-or-flight to regulation before deeper reflection. (Porges, 2011)
pauseScience.reflectDesc: Cognitive reappraisal after regulation leads to better decisions than suppression. (Gross, 2002)
pauseScience.frameDesc: Step back into tools and companions — metacognitive choice about where to look next before you decide. (Flavell, 1979)
pauseScience.breath2Desc: A second regulation pass after reframing lowers arousal again before commitment. (Lehrer & Gevirtz, 2014)
pauseScience.decideDesc: System 2 is now online. You can act from intention, not impulse. (Kahneman, 2011)
